aliases: Czech marinated beef sirloin in cream sauce

winner.title: Svíčková na smetaně

evidence.authenticity: Author is a born-and-raised Czech cook; traditional larded beef, sugar-and-vinegar caramelized root vegetables, spice bundle, roux strained into sauce, cream finish, blended and strained, served with lemon/whipped cream/cranberry. Little history on the page.
evidence.precision: Only 3 of 21 ingredients carry weights, but produce is sized (medium carrots, 7 oz celeriac, 5 oz bacon, 1/3 inch x 4 inch lard strips). 11 steps with sensory cues (golden brown, vinegar evaporated, roux loses floury taste); no oven temps or pan sizes (stovetop, minimal heat, 2.5 h).
evidence.testing: Explains why: discard 1/4 of the vegetables or the sauce turns overly vegetal and dense; count the bay leaves; roux cooked 15 min to lose floury taste; cream added off heat. Rating 4.9 from 28.
evidence.photos: Step photos confirmed via WebFetch for larding, browning, vegetables, roux, thickening, cream, blending and the finished sauce. None in schema.
evidence.efficiency: Single pot, no overnight marinade, 3 h total, realistic.
evidence.access: Parsley root and celeriac are hard to find; the page suggests parsnip and celery, and says parsley can be omitted. Top blade and bacon fat are at any US store.

winner.why: It is the only candidate by a Czech author with a traditional roux-and-cream method, step photos and explained reasoning, while the runner-up has no step photos and a looser sauce method.

runnerUp.title: Svíčková (Braised Beef with Bread Dumplings)

evidence.authenticity: Good history (1805 Prague Cookbook, Bavarian and French influence), but an oven-braise with overnight marinade and a flour-optional sauce.
evidence.precision: Metric and US weights for most items, 320F oven, fork-tender cue, 2 to 4 hours is a wide range.
evidence.testing: Some reasoning and substitution notes (coarse flour = AP flour + semolina 1:1); no test-kitchen sign.
evidence.photos: Ingredient, marinade and finished photos only; no step photos.
evidence.access: Substitutions given for flour, yeast and acid.

runnerUp.why: Strong on history and weights but has no step photos and a less traditional sauce.

companions.title: Svíčková (Braised Beef with Bread Dumplings), dumpling section
companions.why: Yeast bread dumpling with weights, a boil time and a no-slime cue, plus a substitute for Czech coarse flour.

candidates.disqualified: Near word-for-word copy of the Eating Europe recipe; original used instead
